fatal_errors: The proposed electrochemical dealloying method is not the reported spray-drying/thermal decomposition-reduction method.
The initial material is incorrectly described as a bulk HEA ingot rather than spray-dried, compositionally homogeneous mixed-salt precursor particles.
The selective-dissolution mechanism conflicts with the reported hydrogen-assisted sequential reduction and incorporation of transition metals into a noble-metal-seeded lattice.
No synthesis conditions, phase-control variables, or evidence specific to the target study are reconstructed.
The hypothesis predicts a noble-metal-rich residual framework, whereas the target preserves homogeneous multielement high-entropy solid solutions.
explanation: The response recognizes the general objective of producing porous, high-surface-area NM-HEA three-dimensional frameworks and proposes a falsifiable characterization plan. However, it substitutes an established but entirely different fabrication concept. The target method is SD-TDR: homogeneous mixed salts are spray-dried into precursor spheres and reduced in H2, typically at 300°C, causing Pt, Ir, or Ru to nucleate first and catalyze hydrogen-assisted reduction and alloying of Ni, Co, Cu, and Fe. This produces compositionally homogeneous nanoarm-based frameworks without selective element removal. The generated answer also misses the Pt/Ru-dependent fcc–hcp tuning, noble-metal seeding boundaries, Pd and noble-metal-free controls, and methanol-oxidation results. Electrochemical dealloying is chemically plausible in general, but no evidence is supplied that it applies to the paper's system or explains its reported structures.
